stem_book: A rod is arranged at an angle of 30° from the horizontal. Attached to the rod with two strings is the mass m, as shown. The rod is rotated, maintaining its direction in space, so that m travels in a circular path. The strings are of equal length, and make angles of 60° with the rod as shown. Take the length of the strings a = 2.4 m. Calculate the minimum value of the tangential speed (in m/s) of the mass such that the string with tension T 2 does not become slack when the mass is directly above the rod. (Take g = 10 m/s².)
reason: g = 10 m/s² assumed (not printed) | stem: stated g = 10 m/s² (not printed, answer needs it)
work: Along rod: (T₁ − T₂)/2 = mg/2; radial: (T₁ + T₂) sin60° + mg cos30° = mv²/r; T₂ = 0 ⇒ v² = √3·g·r = √3·10·(2.4·√3/2) = 36 ⇒ v = 6 m/s
